opening.text: A backpack on a long hike holds only what you packed. If you packed well, you can walk far. If you didn't, you feel it by the second hill. Self-reliance is about packing well. It is learning to carry what you can, so you can walk with God and help others along the way.

mainMessage.text: Self-reliance is doing what we can, with the Lord's help, so we can grow and bless others.

blocks.text: **Packed for the climb** Good packing is about growing. We grow in body, mind and spirit.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Becoming Self-Reliant” from the October 1991 general conference.
Independence and self-reliance are critical to our spiritual and temporal growth.
Pack for growth.
**More than a program** Self-reliance isn't a checklist. It is a part of the gospel.

Verily I say, men should be anxiously engaged in a good cause, and do many things of their own free will, and bring to pass much righteousness; For the power is in them, wherein they are agents unto themselves. And inasmuch as men do good they shall in nowise lose their reward.
Elder Hugo E. Martinez of the Seventy said this in his talk “Teaching Self-Reliance to Children and Youth” from the April 2022 general conference.
Self-reliance is a doctrine of the gospel of Jesus Christ, not a program.
It is part of the gospel.
**Only what you can carry** A hiker who packs too much gets tired. The Lord knows our limits.

And see that all these things are done in wisdom and order; for it is not requisite that a man should run faster than he has strength. And again, it is expedient that he should be diligent, that thereby he might win the prize; therefore, all things must be done in order.
Bishop W. Christopher Waddell, First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “There Was Bread” from the October 2020 general conference.
The Lord does not expect us to do more than we can do, but He does expect us to do what we can do, when we can do it.
Do what you can.
**One step, then the next** A trail is walked daily. Self-reliance is built day by day.
Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise: Provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest.
Elder Hugo E. Martinez of the Seventy said this in his talk “Teaching Self-Reliance to Children and Youth” from the April 2022 general conference.
It never ends; it is a continuous, daily process.
Keep walking.
**Carrying your own pack** The Lord asks us to carry what we are able to carry. Then He helps with the rest.
Thou shalt not be idle; for he that is idle shall not eat the bread nor wear the garments of the laborer.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Becoming Self-Reliant” from the October 1991 general conference.
He expects His children to be self-reliant to the degree they can be.
Carry what you can.
**Take the first step** The trail doesn't start until someone takes a step. And Christ strengthens that step.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Bishop W. Christopher Waddell, First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “There Was Bread” from the October 2020 general conference.
The most important step of all is to begin.
Begin today.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they learned to do something for themselves, or to provide for their family. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The widow and the oil

blocks.text: A widow was in debt. She had almost nothing. Elisha asked what she had.

And Elisha said unto her, What shall I do for thee? tell me, what hast thou in the house? And she said, Thine handmaid hath not any thing in the house, save a pot of oil. Then she came and told the man of God. And he said, Go, sell the oil, and pay thy debt, and live thou and thy children of the rest.
She had a little oil. That was her start. God asked her to use what she had, and He made it enough.

application.text: First, list what you already have: skills, time, health and friends. Second, choose one small step toward being more self-reliant. Third, take that step this week and ask Heavenly Father to bless it.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God wants His children to grow. I know He blesses our honest work. I know Jesus Christ gives strength to every step we take. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A garden doesn't grow because you wish for it. Someone prepares the soil. Someone plants, waters and pulls weeds. Then, over time, food grows. Self-reliance is a lot like that. It is slow, steady work. And the Lord is in the garden with us.

mainMessage.text: Self-reliance is a garden we tend daily, and God gives the growth.

blocks.text: **Soil and seed** A garden grows a whole life: body, mind and spirit.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Becoming Self-Reliant” from the October 1991 general conference.
Independence and self-reliance are critical to our spiritual and temporal growth.
Grow in every part of life.
**Part of the plan** A gardener follows a plan. Self-reliance is part of God's plan for us.

Verily I say, men should be anxiously engaged in a good cause, and do many things of their own free will, and bring to pass much righteousness; For the power is in them, wherein they are agents unto themselves. And inasmuch as men do good they shall in nowise lose their reward.
Elder Hugo E. Martinez of the Seventy said this in his talk “Teaching Self-Reliance to Children and Youth” from the April 2022 general conference.
Self-reliance is a doctrine of the gospel of Jesus Christ, not a program.
It is part of the plan.
**A garden you can manage** A plot too large becomes a burden. Plant what you can tend.

And see that all these things are done in wisdom and order; for it is not requisite that a man should run faster than he has strength. And again, it is expedient that he should be diligent, that thereby he might win the prize; therefore, all things must be done in order.
Bishop W. Christopher Waddell, First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “There Was Bread” from the October 2020 general conference.
The Lord does not expect us to do more than we can do, but He does expect us to do what we can do, when we can do it.
Tend what you can.
**Water every day** Plants need water daily, not once. Self-reliance is a daily habit.
Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise: Provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest.
Elder Hugo E. Martinez of the Seventy said this in his talk “Teaching Self-Reliance to Children and Youth” from the April 2022 general conference.
It never ends; it is a continuous, daily process.
Water daily.
**Pulling your own weeds** The gardener pulls the weeds. Waiting for rain won't do it. We do our part.
Thou shalt not be idle; for he that is idle shall not eat the bread nor wear the garments of the laborer.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Becoming Self-Reliant” from the October 1991 general conference.
He expects His children to be self-reliant to the degree they can be.
Do your part.
**Plant the first seed** No garden grows from a seed still in the packet. Begin, and trust Christ to strengthen you.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Bishop W. Christopher Waddell, First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “There Was Bread” from the October 2020 general conference.
The most important step of all is to begin.
Plant the seed.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they grew something, learned a skill or got through a lean season. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The widow of Zarephath

blocks.text: A widow was down to her last meal. Elijah asked her to trust God and share.

For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the Lord sendeth rain upon the earth. And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days.
She did her part with what little she had. God did His part, and there was enough every day.

application.text: First, pick one area to tend: food, money, a skill or health. Second, write one thing you will do each day for it. Third, check in with yourself in a week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Heavenly Father helps those who work and trust Him. I know small daily efforts add up. I know Jesus Christ is the source of every good thing that grows. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A sailor can't control the wind. But a sailor can trim the sails and hold the rudder. That is the part that belongs to the sailor. Self-reliance is like that. We don't control every storm. We can learn, work and prepare. And we ask God to fill the sails.

mainMessage.text: Self-reliance is handling the part that is ours, and trusting God with the wind.

blocks.text: **A crew that keeps growing** Good sailors keep learning. We keep growing in every part of life.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Becoming Self-Reliant” from the October 1991 general conference.
Independence and self-reliance are critical to our spiritual and temporal growth.
Keep learning.
**The ship's chart** A ship has a chart. The gospel is ours, and self-reliance is on it.

Verily I say, men should be anxiously engaged in a good cause, and do many things of their own free will, and bring to pass much righteousness; For the power is in them, wherein they are agents unto themselves. And inasmuch as men do good they shall in nowise lose their reward.
Elder Hugo E. Martinez of the Seventy said this in his talk “Teaching Self-Reliance to Children and Youth” from the April 2022 general conference.
Self-reliance is a doctrine of the gospel of Jesus Christ, not a program.
It is on the chart.
**Not too much sail** Too much sail in a storm will tip a boat. The Lord asks only what we can do.

And see that all these things are done in wisdom and order; for it is not requisite that a man should run faster than he has strength. And again, it is expedient that he should be diligent, that thereby he might win the prize; therefore, all things must be done in order.
Bishop W. Christopher Waddell, First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “There Was Bread” from the October 2020 general conference.
The Lord does not expect us to do more than we can do, but He does expect us to do what we can do, when we can do it.
Trim the sail to fit.
**Every day at sea** A voyage is made of many days. Each day, we check the lines and the sails.
Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise: Provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest.
Elder Hugo E. Martinez of the Seventy said this in his talk “Teaching Self-Reliance to Children and Youth” from the April 2022 general conference.
It never ends; it is a continuous, daily process.
Check the lines daily.
**Hand on the rudder** We can't ask someone else to steer our boat. We hold the rudder as far as we are able.
Thou shalt not be idle; for he that is idle shall not eat the bread nor wear the garments of the laborer.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Becoming Self-Reliant” from the October 1991 general conference.
He expects His children to be self-reliant to the degree they can be.
Hold the rudder.
**Leave the dock** A boat that never leaves the dock never sails. Begin, and Christ will strengthen you.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Bishop W. Christopher Waddell, First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “There Was Bread” from the October 2020 general conference.
The most important step of all is to begin.
Leave the dock.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they found a way forward through their own effort and God's help. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Nephi makes a bow

blocks.text: Nephi's steel bow broke. His family was hungry and ready to give up. Nephi didn't give up.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, did make out of wood a bow, and out of a straight stick, an arrow; wherefore, I did arm myself with a bow and an arrow, with a sling and with stones. And I said unto my father: Whither shall I go to obtain food?
Nephi made a new bow with his own hands. Then he asked his father where to go. He worked first, and he asked for direction. Both mattered.

application.text: First, think of a problem you keep waiting on someone else to fix. Second, decide what part of it is yours. Third, do that part, and ask God for direction on the rest.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Heavenly Father gives us direction when we ask and work. I know He doesn't leave us alone in storms. I know Jesus Christ is our strength. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A well holds water only because someone dug it. And it stays full only because someone keeps the rope and bucket in good shape. Nobody expects the water to rise on its own. Self-reliance is the digging and the upkeep. It makes sure there is water when we need it, and some to share.

mainMessage.text: Self-reliance is digging and keeping our own well, so we can drink and give.

blocks.text: **Digging deeper** A well grows deeper over time. So do we, in body, mind and spirit.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Becoming Self-Reliant” from the October 1991 general conference.
Independence and self-reliance are critical to our spiritual and temporal growth.
Go deeper.
**Fed by a spring** A well is fed by a spring beneath it. Self-reliance is fed by the gospel.

Verily I say, men should be anxiously engaged in a good cause, and do many things of their own free will, and bring to pass much righteousness; For the power is in them, wherein they are agents unto themselves. And inasmuch as men do good they shall in nowise lose their reward.
Elder Hugo E. Martinez of the Seventy said this in his talk “Teaching Self-Reliance to Children and Youth” from the April 2022 general conference.
Self-reliance is a doctrine of the gospel of Jesus Christ, not a program.
The gospel is the spring.
**A bucket you can lift** A bucket that is too heavy can't be lifted. The Lord asks what we can carry.

And see that all these things are done in wisdom and order; for it is not requisite that a man should run faster than he has strength. And again, it is expedient that he should be diligent, that thereby he might win the prize; therefore, all things must be done in order.
Bishop W. Christopher Waddell, First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “There Was Bread” from the October 2020 general conference.
The Lord does not expect us to do more than we can do, but He does expect us to do what we can do, when we can do it.
Lift what you can.
**Draw daily** We draw water every day. Self-reliance is not one big effort, but a daily one.
Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise: Provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest.
Elder Hugo E. Martinez of the Seventy said this in his talk “Teaching Self-Reliance to Children and Youth” from the April 2022 general conference.
It never ends; it is a continuous, daily process.
Draw daily.
**Your own rope** Someone else can't haul your bucket forever. We do our share, as far as we can.
Thou shalt not be idle; for he that is idle shall not eat the bread nor wear the garments of the laborer.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Becoming Self-Reliant” from the October 1991 general conference.
He expects His children to be self-reliant to the degree they can be.
Pull your own rope.
**Lower the first bucket** A well is of no use until the bucket goes down. Begin, and Christ will strengthen you.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Bishop W. Christopher Waddell, First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “There Was Bread” from the October 2020 general conference.
The most important step of all is to begin.
Lower the bucket.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they worked hard to meet a need. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Ruth gleans in the field

blocks.text: Ruth and Naomi had no food. Ruth didn't wait to be rescued. She asked to go to work.

And Ruth the Moabitess said unto Naomi, Let me now go to the field, and glean ears of corn after him in whose sight I shall find grace. And she said unto her, Go, my daughter. And she went, and came, and gleaned in the field after the reapers: and her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech.
Ruth worked hard, in humble work, for her family. And she was led to the right field. God opens doors for those who go to work.

application.text: First, think of a need in your home that you can meet yourself. Second, take one small action toward it this week. Third, thank Heavenly Father for the strength to do it.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Heavenly Father honors honest effort. I know He leads us to the right door when we go to work. I know Jesus Christ lifts what we can't lift alone. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Think of a pantry. A few cans, some rice, a bag of flour. It isn't fancy. But on a hard week, it means a family can eat without panic. Self-reliance is a lot like a pantry. We fill it a little at a time, before we need it. Then, when hard days come, we are ready.

mainMessage.text: Self-reliance is filling the shelves a little at a time, so we are ready and can help others.

blocks.text: **Shelves for every need** Our shelves hold more than food. They hold learning, health and faith.
And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Becoming Self-Reliant” from the October 1991 general conference.
Independence and self-reliance are critical to our spiritual and temporal growth.
Stock every shelf.
**Part of the gospel** A pantry is not a project to finish. It is a way of living the gospel.

Verily I say, men should be anxiously engaged in a good cause, and do many things of their own free will, and bring to pass much righteousness; For the power is in them, wherein they are agents unto themselves. And inasmuch as men do good they shall in nowise lose their reward.
Elder Hugo E. Martinez of the Seventy said this in his talk “Teaching Self-Reliance to Children and Youth” from the April 2022 general conference.
Self-reliance is a doctrine of the gospel of Jesus Christ, not a program.

Add what you can.

Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise: Provideth her meat in the summer, and gathereth her food in the harvest.
Elder Hugo E. Martinez of the Seventy said this in his talk “Teaching Self-Reliance to Children and Youth” from the April 2022 general conference.
It never ends; it is a continuous, daily process.
A little each day.
**Your own shelves** We do our own stocking, as far as we are able. And we are glad to share what we have.
Thou shalt not be idle; for he that is idle shall not eat the bread nor wear the garments of the laborer.
Elder L. Tom Perry of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Becoming Self-Reliant” from the October 1991 general conference.
He expects His children to be self-reliant to the degree they can be.
Stock your own.
**Buy the first can** A pantry begins with one item. Begin, and Christ will strengthen you.
I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.
Bishop W. Christopher Waddell, First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “There Was Bread” from the October 2020 general conference.
The most important step of all is to begin.
Begin with one.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when being prepared made a hard week easier. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Joseph stores the grain

blocks.text: Joseph was told seven good years would be followed by seven hard ones. He didn't wait.

And he gathered up all the food of the seven years, which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities: the food of the field, which was round about every city, laid he up in the same. And Joseph gathered corn as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left numbering; for it was without number.
He prepared in the good years. When the hard years came, there was food, and others were fed too. Preparing is a way of loving people before they need it.

application.text: First, look at your own pantry, savings or skills. Second, pick one thing to add this month. Third, keep a little aside for someone else.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Heavenly Father prepares a way when we prepare. I know small steady habits bring peace. I know Jesus Christ is the foundation of every good preparation. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
